A method of determining reserved tones for reduction of a peak to average power ratio (PAPR) includes: selecting carrier indices for the reserved tones and generating a kernel signal based on the selected carrier indices; calculating a comparison reference average value of the kernel signal, selecting one of the calculated comparison reference average value and a prestored comparison reference average value, and preliminarily determining carrier indices of the reserved tones based on the selection; re-arranging an order of the preliminarily determined carrier indices; calculating a comparison reference average value of a kernel signal generated, whenever each of the re-arranged carrier indices is changed to another carrier index, to generate a plurality of comparison reference average values, and finally determining carrier indices of the reserved tones which generates a kernel signal having the smallest comparison reference average value among the comparison reference average values as the indices of the reserved tones.

outputs.L2: A technique for identifying reserved tones to lower the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) involves choosing carrier indices to serve as the reserved tones and producing a kernel signal from those chosen indices. A comparison reference average value for the kernel signal is then computed, and either this computed value or a previously stored comparison reference average value is selected. Based on that selection, the carrier indices for the reserved tones are provisionally identified. The order of these provisionally identified carrier indices is then rearranged. Each rearranged carrier index is, in turn, replaced with another carrier index, and for each replacement, a comparison reference average value is calculated for the resulting kernel signal, thereby producing multiple comparison reference average values. Finally, the carrier indices that produce the kernel signal with the lowest comparison reference average value among all the calculated values are selected as the final reserved tone indices.

The method is used to determine reserved tones for reducing a peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) in a multicarrier transmission signal.

First, a set of carrier indices is selected as candidates for the reserved tones. Based on these selected carrier indices, a kernel signal is generated. The kernel signal represents the effect that the selected reserved tones may have when used for PAPR reduction.

Next, a comparison reference average value of the generated kernel signal is calculated. This comparison reference average value is then compared with a prestored reference value. Based on the result of this comparison, the method preliminarily determines a set of reserved tone carrier indices.

After the preliminary reserved tone carrier indices are determined, the method further optimizes the selection. The preliminarily determined carrier indices are re-arranged, and each carrier index is individually changed to another carrier index. For each rearranged or modified set of carrier indices, a corresponding kernel signal is generated, and a corresponding comparison reference average value is calculated.

The comparison reference average values obtained from the different candidate sets are then compared with one another. Finally, the reserved tone carrier indices are selected as the set of indices that produces the kernel signal having the smallest comparison reference average value. By selecting the reserved tones in this manner, the method identifies carrier indices that are more effective for reducing PAPR.

A method for determining reserved tones for reducing a peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) in a multicarrier transmission system is provided. The method may be applied, for example, to an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signal in which some carrier tones are reserved and are not used for transmitting user data. Instead, the reserved tones are used to generate a peak-cancelling signal that reduces the peak power of a time-domain transmission waveform.

In the method, a plurality of carrier indices are first selected from among carrier indices available in a frequency-domain transmission band. Each carrier index corresponds to a carrier tone or subcarrier that may be used as a candidate reserved tone. For the selected carrier indices, kernel signals are generated. A kernel signal may represent a time-domain signal component corresponding to one or more candidate reserved tones, and may be used to evaluate how effectively the corresponding carrier index or set of carrier indices can contribute to PAPR reduction.

For each candidate carrier index or each candidate combination of carrier indices, a comparison reference average value is obtained. The comparison reference average value may be calculated from the generated kernel signal, or may be retrieved from a previously stored table or database. The comparison reference average value is a metric used to compare the PAPR-reduction effectiveness of different candidate reserved-tone arrangements. For example, the value may be based on an average magnitude, an average power, or another statistical measure of the kernel signal.

Based on the comparison reference average values, a preliminary set of reserved-tone indices is selected. The preliminary set includes carrier indices that are expected to provide favorable PAPR reduction performance. After the preliminary reserved-tone indices are chosen, the indices may be reordered according to the corresponding comparison reference average values or according to another predetermined ordering rule. This reordering allows the method to identify which reserved-tone indices are more important or less important for the PAPR reduction performance.

The method then performs an iterative substitution process. During this process, at least one carrier index included in the preliminary reserved-tone set is replaced with another carrier index that is not currently included in the reserved-tone set. A new kernel signal is generated or identified for the modified set of reserved-tone indices, and a corresponding comparison reference average value is computed or retrieved. The comparison reference average value of the modified set is then compared with that of the current reserved-tone set.

If the substitution results in a kernel signal having a smaller comparison reference average value, the substituted carrier index is retained as part of the reserved-tone set. If the substitution does not improve the comparison reference average value, the previous carrier index may be restored, and another substitution may be tested. This process may be repeated for multiple carrier indices and multiple candidate substitutions until a predetermined stopping condition is satisfied. The stopping condition may include, for example, completion of testing for all candidate carrier indices, reaching a predetermined number of iterations, or determining that no further improvement is obtained.

After the iterative testing is completed, the reserved tones are finalized. The finalized reserved tones correspond to the carrier indices that produce a kernel signal having the smallest comparison reference average value among the tested candidates. By selecting reserved tones in this manner, the system can identify tones that are more effective in generating a peak-reduction signal. As a result, the PAPR of the multicarrier transmission signal can be reduced more efficiently, improving transmission performance and reducing the burden on power amplifiers and other radio-frequency transmission components.
outputs.L5:
**PAPR (Peak-to-Average Power Ratio)** is an important concept in modern communication systems, especially in multicarrier transmission techniques such as OFDM (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing). It refers to the ratio between the maximum instantaneous power of a signal and its average power.

In simple terms, PAPR shows how much the signal peaks rise above its normal average level. A high PAPR means that the signal occasionally has very large peaks. This can be a problem because power amplifiers in transmitters must handle these peaks without distortion. If the amplifier is not operated with enough power back-off, the peaks may be clipped, causing signal distortion, increased bit errors, and interference with neighboring channels.

PAPR is commonly expressed in decibels (dB):

\[
PAPR = 10 \log_{10}\left(\frac{P_{peak}}{P_{avg}}\right)
\]

High PAPR is a major drawback of OFDM systems because many subcarriers can add together constructively, creating large signal peaks. To reduce this issue, several PAPR reduction techniques are used, including clipping, coding, selected mapping, partial transmit sequence, and tone reservation.

Reducing PAPR improves power efficiency, allows better use of power amplifiers, and enhances overall system performance. For this reason, PAPR remains an important topic in wireless communication, 4G, 5G, digital broadcasting, and other high-speed data transmission systems.

## Technical Patent Summary: PAPR Reduction Using Adaptive Reserved-Tone Selection Based on Kernel-Signal Average Value

A peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction technique is disclosed for a multicarrier communication system, such as an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system. The technique reduces transmit-signal peaks by adaptively selecting and finalizing reserved tones used for peak cancellation.

In one implementation, a transmitter initially identifies a plurality of candidate reserved tones among available subcarriers. These tones are not used for payload data transmission and are instead allocated for generating a peak-reduction or cancellation signal. The preliminarily selected reserved tones may be chosen according to predetermined tone-location rules, channel conditions, tone spacing constraints, or system configuration parameters.

After preliminary selection, the reserved tones are reordered. The reordering may be performed according to tone index, frequency position, contribution to peak suppression, correlation with time-domain peak locations, or another optimization metric. The reordered reserved tones are then processed individually. For each reserved tone, a corresponding kernel signal is generated in the time domain. The kernel signal represents the time-domain response or peak-cancellation contribution produced when the respective reserved tone is activated or modified.

Each reserved tone is individually changed, adjusted, or evaluated by altering one or more parameters associated with the tone, such as phase, amplitude, complex weighting coefficient, or inclusion status. For each candidate change, a kernel signal is generated or updated, and an average value of the generated kernel signal is determined. The average value may represent an average magnitude, average power, mean absolute value, or another statistical measure of the kernel signal over a time-domain symbol interval.

A final reserved-tone set is determined based on the minimum average value among the generated kernel signals. In particular, the system selects or finalizes the reserved tone or tone configuration that produces the lowest average kernel-signal value, thereby providing an efficient cancellation signal with reduced energy overhead while maintaining effective PAPR suppression. By selecting reserved tones according to the minimum average value of the generated kernel signal, the method can improve peak reduction performance, reduce distortion, and limit the power allocated to non-data tones.

The finalized reserved tones are then used to generate a peak-reduction signal that is combined with the original multicarrier transmit signal. The resulting transmit waveform has a reduced PAPR compared with the original waveform, improving power amplifier efficiency and reducing nonlinear distortion.

The disclosed technique may be implemented in a base station, user equipment, wireless modem, OFDM transmitter, digital front-end processor, or integrated circuit. The method is applicable to various multicarrier systems, including OFDM, OFDMA, DMT, and other systems employing tone reservation for PAPR reduction.
